names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 16 Απριλίου, «Άγιος Λεωνίδης και οι Αγίες Χάρισσα, Νίκη, Γαλήνη, Καλλίδα, Νουνεχία, Βασίλισσα και Θεοδώρα», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's heading for the Julian 16 April, „Св. муч. Леонид и с њим мученице: Хариеса, Никија, Галина, Калида, Нунехија, Василиса и Теодора.“, with Св. left off — it is not a rank — and without муч. and мученице, which are the `martyr` this folder already carries in `types`. One rank word stands over the whole company and belongs to none of them, so what is left for this saint is the bare forename; the heading gives no epithet, no city and no see, and the companionship clause this corpus keeps in some of these display names is not part of the source's name for anybody. No other folder in the corpus holds this Serbian form.

Read out of the title on the name link behind the line for 16 апреля ст. ст., name page 2745, with the rank word left off; the day's own line gives the name in the genitive, «Хариессы». No folder in this corpus holds this form, and the gate's key for it has no other holder, measured. The name page prints «Хариесса (Харисса)» in the title of the article it links; the head form is the one taken.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 16 апреля ст. ст. — «Мч. Леонида и мцц. Хариессы , Ники , Галины , Калисы , Нунехии , Василиссы , Феодоры , Ирины и иных (258).»
source.note: The day's second entry, which names her among the seven women the Greek and Serbian rows this folder already carries name. The name page behind the line gives «День памяти: 16 апреля» and no other day. It carries no typikon icon, so no `rank` is recorded; the day's one icon stands before the first entry, and neither of the day's two hymns is this company's. **The line's year is 258, where the Greek page this folder already cites puts the martyrdom in the reign of Decius, 249 to 251**; this folder's interval, 249 to 281, holds both, so `dates` were not touched. The line also closes the company with «и иных» — and others — who are not named and have no folder. **This calendar's name page for every one of the nine serves a second life besides the company's own: the life of a martyr of Corinth under Decius and of the disciples who gathered to him, two of whom were drowned in the sea and one of those called Леонид.** That is the calendar's own grouping of two dossiers under one name and it is recorded here as such; no identification was made by this reader. The same name pages print a teaser for an article on Православие.Ru which makes Leonid the leader of a women's choir arrested at Troezen; an article is not the calendar's life, nothing has been taken from it, and it is named in the report.

attestations.note: Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 16ης Απριλίου — «Άγιος Λεωνίδης και οι Αγίες Χάρισσα, Νίκη, Γαλήνη, Καλλίδα, Νουνεχία, Βασίλισσα και Θεοδώρα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 16 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. Eight names in one line, each with a couplet of its own, so eight folders; hers is «Eις την Xάρισσαν». The page gives no year: it sets them only «στα χρόνια του βασιλιά Δεκίου (249 - 251 μ.Χ.)», a reign and not a date, so there is no `dates` object. The corpus holds nobody of this name. The page prints no hymn in full.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 29.04.2026 (16. април ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Леонид и с њим мученице: Хариеса, Никија, Галина, Калида, Нунехија, Василиса и Теодора.“

attestations.note: The day's second entry, an enumerated company of eight — Leonides and seven women named one after another — so one row each, on the same menologion day the Greek keeps them on. The entry is four lines and tells only the end, and it tells it as a wonder the Greek page has nothing of: the sea would not receive them, they walked on it as on dry land singing to God, the pagans marvelled and then tied stones about their necks and threw them into the deep a second time. **It also gives a year, and the year is a disagreement**: „Сви чесно пострадаше за Христа Цара и Господа 281. год.“, where saint.gr — the source this folder was written from — puts the company in the years of the king Decius and dates that reign 249 to 251. Neither reading is chosen: the folder's `dates` now carries the whole of the disagreement as one interval and its note names both, which is what docs/CORPUS.md §3 asks for. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion, and the martyrs' song in the entry is the entry's own narrative and not a hymn of the Church.

death.note: Two sources that disagree, recorded as one interval and nothing chosen, on docs/CORPUS.md §3's rule. The Ohrid Prologue for 16. април ст. ст. closes the entry „Сви чесно пострадаше за Христа Цара и Господа 281. год.“ — all suffered honourably for Christ the King and Lord in the year 281. saint.gr, the source this folder was written from and quoted in its own Greek row, instead puts the company in the years of the king Decius and dates that reign 249 to 251, thirty years earlier. The folder held no `dates` before this, so nothing was narrowed and nothing displaced; the lower bound is the Greek reading's earliest year and the upper bound the Serbian reading's only year. No year of birth is recorded anywhere read.
